rules.title: Statewide prohibition on local rent control, with narrow exception (M.G.L. c. 40P, § 4)
rules.requirement: No Massachusetts city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind. The only exception is for a city or town that accepts the chapter, which may adopt rent control that becomes voluntary for owners after six months, excludes small-portfolio and higher-rent units, and requires the municipality to compensate owners for the gap between fair market rent and controlled rent.
rules.key_value: Local rent control prohibited; any permitted local scheme must be voluntary after 6 months, exclude owners of fewer than 10 rental units and units with fair market rent over $400, and compensate owners from general funds
rules.quoted_span: Section 4. No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all cities and towns in Massachusetts. Any permitted local rent control may not apply to any rental unit owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units, or to any unit with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.exemptions: Permitted local regulation may not apply to units owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units, or to units with fair market rent exceeding $400. It may not regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from regulation. Owner compliance becomes entirely voluntary six months after initial adoption.
rules.interaction: This state law preempts local rent control. Municipalities may adopt rent control only under the restrictive conditions of the section, including municipal compensation to owners funded from general funds.
